title: FactCandidatePlan
description: The PROSE-TO-FACT candidate plan (roadmap Phase 5, Fact Candidate Pipeline). A serial novel grows facts as it is written: chapter prose reveals a character's new ability, a location, an age — knowledge the authored Registry does not yet hold. Without a channel back, the fact layer (and every projection folded from it: Character Runtime, Story State, Timeline) drifts behind the prose over a long serial. This artifact is the PREPARATION half of the closed loop: it EXTRACTS candidate facts from a produced ChapterDraft (a derived prose artifact) and RECONCILES each against the current Registry, classifying it as new / additive / consistent / conflicting / unverifiable. It is written to registry/derived/fact-candidates/, NEVER to registry/facts/ (a candidate is not yet a fact, ADR-006). Extraction is generative/evaluative (a model reads prose) and NEVER gates; reconciliation-classification is DETERMINISTIC (a candidate value either matches, extends, contradicts, or cannot be compared against a declared fact). The plan MUST NOT auto-resolve a conflict: a contradiction between prose and an existing fact is surfaced for a human to judge (prose typo? retcon? new fact superseding old?), because auto-overwriting the SSOT from inference is exactly the rot ADR-006 forbids. Two structural invariants: `gating` const false — a candidate plan NEVER blocks a build (ADR-003); and `authority` const human — minting a candidate into registry/facts/ is an irreversible SSOT transition, so the system may prepare/stage but only a human authorizes the mint (ADR-009). This schema deliberately stops at the boundary: it stages candidates; the mint executor (which writes facts and bumps fact_version) and the derived recompute it triggers are SEPARATE workflows, described in `next_workflow` but not performed here.

authority.description: Structural invariant (ADR-009): promoting a candidate into registry/facts/ is an irreversible SSOT transition. The system prepares and stages this plan; only a human authorizes the mint. The plan's mere existence is never consent.

gating.description: Structural invariant (ADR-003): a candidate plan NEVER blocks a build. Extraction is a model reading prose (evaluative); the deterministic reconciliation only classifies, it does not gate.

review_status.description: Mirrors runtime/outline/import_plan.py: a staged plan is inert until a human reviews it. Only value permitted at stage time.

writes_registry_facts.description: Structural invariant: staging a candidate plan writes ONLY a derived artifact, never registry/facts/. Enforced by an architecture-fitness guard on the candidates subdomain.

requires_id_mint_review.description: A `new` candidate needs a real minted ID (the temporary CAND-* id is not an SSOT id); minting is a separate human-authorized workflow paired with the ID Mint Ledger.

source.description: The produced prose this plan extracted candidates FROM. Pinning the draft's content_hash makes the plan reproducible and lets a consumer detect that the prose it was extracted from has since changed.

chapter_draft_id.description: The ChapterDraft derived-artifact id (e.g. its task_id).

content_hash.description: The draft's content_hash at extraction time (sha256:...).

extractor.description: Which extractor produced the raw candidates: 'deterministic' (CI stub) or a model id. Extraction is evaluative; this records provenance, it does not gate.

reconciled_against.description: The fact pins (ID@vN) each candidate was deterministically classified against, at the Registry version this plan was staged at. This is the plan's own `derived_from`: if any of these facts advances before the plan is minted, the plan is STALE (runtime/derived.py) and must be re-run — you must not mint from a reconciliation computed against superseded facts.

items.description: One entry per candidate fact extracted from the prose, each carrying its deterministic reconciliation classification.

candidate_id.description: A TEMPORARY plan-local id. NOT an SSOT id — a `new` candidate gets a real minted id only when a human authorizes the mint (ADR-009 + ID Mint Ledger).

classification.description: The DETERMINISTIC reconciliation verdict. new = no matching entity; additive = matches an entity, the field is currently empty (extends it, bumps fact_version); consistent = matches an entity and the value equals the declared fact (confirmation only, low signal); conflicting = matches an entity and the value CONTRADICTS the declared fact (NEVER auto-resolved — routed to a human); unverifiable = free text that cannot be deterministically compared to a declared fact (routed to a human).

target_type.description: Entity type the candidate is about (Character, Event, WorldRule, ...), by catalog.

matched_entity_id.description: For additive/consistent/conflicting: the existing fact id this candidate reconciles against. Absent for `new`.

field.description: The fact field the candidate asserts (e.g. physical_facts.eye_color, abilities).

extracted_value.description: The value the prose asserts (any JSON type).

existing_value.description: For additive/consistent/conflicting: the current declared value in facts (null/absent shows why `additive`). Present so a reviewer sees prose-vs-fact side by side.

confidence.description: Extractor's confidence (evaluative, advisory). Never gates and never changes a deterministic classification; it only helps a human triage.

evidence.description: The prose span (a short quote) the candidate was extracted from. Grounds the reviewer's judgement — especially for a `conflicting` item, where they must decide prose-typo vs retcon vs new-fact-supersedes-old.

reason.description: Human-readable note on why this classification / why routed to review.

next_workflow.description: What happens AFTER a human reviews this plan — described, never performed here (ADR-009 preparation/execution split). Records the boundary so no reader mistakes staging for minting.

mint.description: The human-authorized mint step: accepted new/additive candidates are written to registry/facts/ and fact_version is bumped. A separate workflow, paired with the ID Mint Ledger.

recompute.description: After a mint, derived artifacts pinned to the changed facts go stale and must be recomputed. A separate workflow (Derived Recompute Engine).

rationale.description: Human-readable summary of what the plan found (counts per classification, notable conflicts).
